newsitem.title: UK: Replace royal yacht, British government urged.
newsitem.headline: Replace royal yacht, British government urged.

text.p: Supporters of a replacement for the Royal Yacht Britannia appealed to the British government on Thursday to stop dithering and build a successor to the ship in time for the Millennium celebrations.

The all-party Royal Yacht Parliamentary Group, backed by British exporters' groups, said Britannia was a unique asset that had more than paid its way by helping secure two billion pounds ($3.35 billion) of exports for Britain over the past decade.
But ministers, fearing a taxpayers' backlash, are reluctant to decide before the coming election whether to replace Britannia, which could cost as much as 100 million pounds.
Britannia, a sleek 6,000-tonne mini-luxury liner that costs about 10 million pounds a year to run, sails next Monday on its final voyage. It is due to be taken out of service after 44 years afloat.

Michael Colvin, the Conservative chairman of the House of Commons defence committee, blamed "the dead hand of the Treasury" and the negative image of some members of the Royal family for the government's hesitations.
Conservative peer Lord Edward Ashbourne said he envisaged Britannia's replacement as a "workhorse for Britain" that would be a floating royal palace and a powerful export promotion tool.
Ashbourne said the new ship should be funded mainly by the government. Queen Elizabeth, he said, was not keen on a commercially funded yacht.
"She has a vision of (the logo of chemical giant) ICI on the funnel, which would not be in keeping with the ambience of the Royal Yacht," he said.
Gail Murdoch, export director of British Invisibles, which represents British business and financial institutions, said the Britannia generated tremendous interest whenever it visited foreign ports.
"Our members are very supportive and would certainly like to see a new Royal Yacht. It's a national asset, a unique forum and much envied by our competitors," she said.

Britannia will sail next week via the Gulf and the Indian Ocean for Hong Kong. Prince Charles is to embark with Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten after the colony's ceremonial handover to China on June 30. ($1=.5976 Pound)
